priorities.name: Private space for sensitive meetings and all-day calls
priorities.issue: Associates on sensitive-topic meetings lack all-day private space, and meeting-heavy calendars make the quiet zones hard to actually use.
whatItLooksLike: Lack of offices in which I can work all day. I am on meetings on sensitive topics, and working in general areas is not appropriate.
Too much noise and distraction at times. So many meetings on our calendar it's hard to utilize the Quiet Zones.

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (82/100); discretion-space friction 28/100 (51% under-supported).
Privacy & Confidentiality: 162 people (23% of respondents), 224 comments, 64% negative; Noise & Distraction: 160 people (23% of respondents), 205 comments, 67% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Assess enclosed/quiet-space capacity against the meeting-heavy demand pattern; review whether quiet zones are being absorbed by meetings and need protection or expansion.
priorities.siteMustDo: Measure private-room demand vs. availability across a typical week and escalate the capacity gap with evidence.

priorities.name: Desk reservations and booking window
priorities.issue: The two-week booking window is too short for how associates plan, and reservations are the highest-volume complaint at the largest site.
whatItLooksLike: Reservations should be available more than 2 weeks out. It is very inconvenient that we can only schedule 2 weeks at a time.

evidence.text: Desk Availability & Reservations: 147 people (21% of respondents), 186 comments, 48% negative — Physical Environment is the #2 priority category (76/100).

priorities.proposedAction: Review the booking-window policy (is the 2-week limit local or enterprise?) and no-show handling.
priorities.siteMustDo: Confirm whether the 2-week window is a local setting or enterprise policy, and route accordingly.

priorities.name: Workstation equipment and connectivity reliability
priorities.issue: Monitors and video often don't work, and USB-C cords on specific floors fail to connect to the network — the site's Digital & Tech score is the lowest of all sites.
whatItLooksLike: Often the monitors don't work and occasionally the video meetings don't work.
Many of the USBC cords don't work and allow you to connect to the network on the 4th floor.

evidence.text: Hardware: 176 people (26% of respondents), 237 comments, 61% negative; Connectivity: 131 people (19% of respondents), 162 comments, 57% negative.
Digital & Tech dimension is 69.9 ± 1, below the company average (72.0).

priorities.proposedAction: Run a floor-by-floor equipment and cable audit (the 4th-floor USB-C issue is specific and testable) and route confirmed faults to Technology.
priorities.siteMustDo: Audit cords/monitors by floor, replace failed cables, and escalate the connectivity pattern to Technology with locations.

priorities.name: Thermal comfort (temperature)
priorities.issue: The office is widely described as too cold — desks beneath supply vents especially — and it is one of the most frequent and most negative complaints at the site.
whatItLooksLike: It is always too cold in the office which makes it uncomfortable. …
The temperature is always frigid and even though I bring a jacket or sweater to wear, my hands are so cold it is difficult to even type. …
…The desks beneath a vent can be freezing cold & I'm typically hot.

evidence.text: Temperature / Thermal: 117 people (17% of respondents), 130 comments, 77% negative.
Thermal / temperature comfort: Under Supported — friction 23/100 (46% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Have Workplace Operations map cold zones — starting with desks under supply vents — and check set-points, airflow balancing and diffuser direction in those zones.
priorities.siteMustDo: Log cold zones and times by floor for two weeks, submit them to building operations, and verify the corrections hold.

priorities.name: Chair comfort and sit/stand desk repairs
priorities.issue: Chairs are uncomfortable and hard to re-adjust at each new desk, and some standing desks in offices are broken.
whatItLooksLike: The chairs are very uncomfortable and hurt my back. …
I have back issues and adjusting the chairs each time in a new cubicle is not easy
The standing desks in some of the offices are broken.

evidence.text: Furniture & Ergonomics: 56 people (8% of respondents), 58 comments, 64% negative.
Furniture comfort & ergonomics: Under Supported — friction 14/100 (34% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Audit chair and sit/stand desk condition, fix broken standing desks, and post simple chair-adjustment guidance at shared desks; assess a chair upgrade only if the audit shows widespread wear.
priorities.siteMustDo: Complete the chair and desk audit by floor, repair what is broken, and report the scale of any remaining gap.
